families.page_title: Chloroform: health effects, incident management and toxicology
evidence_points: The official UKHSA page provides information on chloroform, also known as trichloromethane or methyl trichloride for use in responding to chemical incidents.
The page is published by the UK Health Security Agency on GOV.UK.
The publication was first published on 30 July 2014.
The GOV.UK record shows a latest update of 6 August 2024.
The publication provides general information, incident management and toxicological overview material.
The linked material describes health effects associated with exposure to chloroform, also known as trichloromethane or methyl trichloride.
The source provides substance-specific incident-response information rather than treating all chemical events as equivalent.
The official page was live-opened successfully on 31 July 2026 and retained its current GOV.UK publication title.
An alert, symptom, exposure report, incident notification or checklist alone does not establish that every recommendation on Chloroform: health effects, incident management and toxicology applies.

Final decisions require the current official page scope plus the exact substance, exposure route, concentration or quantity, duration, affected people, setting, measurements, clinical and operational evidence, responsible organisations, protective actions, communication, documentation and review.
